snippet.title: Prison Moms: The World's Worst Place To Raise A Child?
snippet.description:
When Britney Crozier was sentenced to 13 years for drug trafficking, her biggest fear wasn’t the prison walls—it was losing her children forever. For thousands of incarcerated mothers, a long sentence usually means the end of motherhood. But inside the Grand Valley Institution for Women, a radical and highly controversial experiment is challenging everything we know about crime, punishment, and family.

From recorded bedtime storybooks that keep long-distance bonds alive, to the high-stakes Mother-Child Program where infants literally grow up behind bars, this documentary pulls back the curtain on the hidden world of prison parenting.

Is allowing a baby to live in a correctional facility a breakthrough for rehabilitation, or is it a psychological risk for the child? Can an incarcerated mother truly break a multi-generational cycle of crime when her own mother was in the system?

We follow Britney, her father Ed (who has suddenly become a full-time caregiver in his 50s), and former inmates who credit their time parenting behind bars as the only reason they chose sobriety over a life of crime. This is a raw, unfiltered look at guilt, accountability, and the fierce power of a mother's love in the darkest of places.

snippet.title: The Hidden Spy Intelligence War Between NATO And The Soviets | Full Documentary
snippet.description:
During the Cold War, divided Germany became a battlefield for spies with diplomatic passports. The Allied Military Liaison Missions were created after World War Two to maintain contact between occupying powers, but by the 1960s and 1980s they had become a legal cover for dangerous reconnaissance behind the Iron Curtain. British, French and American officers roamed East Germany, counting tanks, photographing Soviet bases, stealing equipment and tracking military trains while the Stasi watched every move. This documentary follows the secret intelligence war from the Berlin Wall in 1961 and John F. Kennedy’s 1963 West Berlin speech to the betrayals of Heinz Felfe and John Walker. It reveals how the KGB, Stasi, NATO and Western military missions fought a hidden war of surveillance, blackmail and counterintelligence. The danger turns deadly in 1984, when French mission driver Philippe Mariotti is killed during a Stasi trap, exposing the human cost of Cold War espionage.

snippet.title: Louis Theroux Explores The Extremely High Cost Of End Of Life Care in America
snippet.description:
Louis visits LA's most famous hospital, the Cedars-Sinai Medical Centre in West Hollywood, where he meets patients battling for their lives against serious illnesses.

America spends a huge amount on health care and a hefty proportion goes on end of life care, with a wide and expensive array of treatments on offer to those with insurance or who qualify for government funded programmes. Louis talks to patients and their families as they face some of the toughest decisions imaginable - whether to accept death and die in relative comfort, or to gamble on further, possibly painful treatment in the hope that it will cure them or prolong their life. He also talks to the doctors whose job it is to guide people through this traumatic process.

Over several months Louis explores the American way of death, which often involves never giving up and keeping faith right to the end.

snippet.title: Measuring the Unmeasurable: The Great Wall's True Dimensions | Full Documentary
snippet.description:
It is the largest structure ever built by human hands. It stretches across 15 provinces, crosses deserts, mountains, and plunges into the sea. Walking from one end to the other, eight hours a day, would take two full years. And yet, for all its fame, most of what the Great Wall of China truly is remains hidden. Sections buried under the Gobi Desert for centuries. Construction techniques that turned ordinary earth into something harder than stone. A secret ingredient, hiding in plain sight in every Chinese kitchen, that made the mortar stronger with every passing decade. Using satellite radar, drone technology, and molecular-level analysis, scientists are now uncovering a structure far older, far longer, and far more ingeniously built than anyone previously imagined. The official length was revised from 6,700 km to over 21,000 km. Some researchers believe the real figure could be 50,000 km. The Great Wall of China is not what you think it is.

snippet.title: Hitler’s Cultural Purge: Art and Media Under Nazi Rule | Full Documentary
snippet.description:
He was a failed artist who couldn't paint people. Rejected twice by the Vienna Academy of Fine Arts, Adolf Hitler never forgot the humiliation. When he came to power, his revenge wasn't just political. It was cultural. Within years, every artist, writer, musician, filmmaker, and architect in Germany had to register with the state, prove their racial identity, and conform to a single, centrally controlled vision of what art was allowed to be. Those who refused lost their licence to work. Those who couldn't comply fled. The rest were watched. What followed was one of the most sophisticated and terrifying propaganda systems ever constructed, built not on screaming speeches alone, but on cinema, radio, architecture, and the deliberate manipulation of taste. And at the centre of it all was a question that nobody in the regime could agree on: what does Nazi art actually look like?

Within years, every artist, writer, musician, filmmaker, and architect in Germany had to register with the state, prove their racial identity, and conform to a single, centrally controlled vision of what art was allowed to be. Those who refused lost their licence to work. Those who couldn't comply fled. The rest were watched. What followed was one of the most sophisticated and terrifying propaganda systems ever constructed, built not on screaming speeches alone, but on cinema, radio, architecture, and the deliberate manipulation of taste. And at the centre of it all was a question that nobody in the regime could agree on: what does Nazi art actually look like?

snippet.description:
After the division of Germany in 1949, East Germany became one of the most important military zones of the Cold War. Nowhere else in Europe could NATO observe the Soviet military so closely, often just meters away from the border.

Throughout the 1950s to the 1980s, intelligence agents, reconnaissance teams, and informants operated along the Iron Curtain, gathering critical information about troop movements and military capabilities. At the same time, the KGB worked to infiltrate NATO and Western governments, turning espionage into a constant battle of observation and deception. This story reveals how East Germany became the central frontline of a hidden war where information was the most powerful weapon.

snippet.title: From Caltrops To Mines: The Evolution Of Ambush Weapons | Full Documentary
snippet.description:
Ambush warfare has been a decisive tactic for centuries, allowing smaller or weaker forces to defeat stronger opponents through surprise and positioning. From ancient battlefields to modern conflicts, weapons designed to remain hidden until the last moment have transformed the way wars are fought. Early tools like caltrops, used as far back as antiquity, could stop cavalry charges and control entire battlefields by making terrain impassable.

With the development of firearms in the 18th and 19th centuries, soldiers gained the ability to fire rifles from a prone position, increasing accuracy while staying concealed. In the 20th century, the introduction of land mines added a new level of danger, creating invisible threats that could strike at any time. This story explores how ambush tactics evolved over time, combining technology and strategy to create some of the most effective and feared methods of warfare.

snippet.title: Steps To The Future: Cosmic Hazards
snippet.description:
Could a cosmic event wipe out humanity tomorrow? Discover the hidden threats from space—magnetars, gamma ray bursts, and asteroid impacts—that could shape Earth's fate.

Journey deep into cosmic dangers and Earth's turbulent history in this eye-opening exploration of existential risks facing our planet. From the mysterious power of magnetars to catastrophic gamma ray bursts and lethal asteroid impacts like Apophis, this video dives into the cutting-edge science behind humanity’s greatest cosmic threats. Learn how the Earth’s magnetic field shields us from solar and cosmic radiation, and what could happen if it falters or reverses. See how massive volcanic eruptions and celestial impacts have triggered past mass extinctions, including the one that ended the dinosaurs—and what this tells us about the next possible global disaster.

Through expert interviews, laboratory experiments, and stunning field research, we reveal how phenomena like climate change, magnetic field shifts, and recurring ice ages are influenced by planetary motions and cosmic forces far beyond human control. Will rising carbon dioxide emissions protect us from another ice age or doom us to environmental collapse? What are humanity’s real odds against a civilization-ending gamma ray burst or an asteroid striking Earth? Explore the history of life’s resilience in the face of planetary upheavals and the creative power hidden in cosmic destruction.

If you’ve ever wondered about our planet’s fragility, survival, and cosmic destiny, this documentary will both awe and challenge your understanding of what it means to live on Earth.

snippet.title: Surviving America's Most Extreme Prison for Children
snippet.description:
For many troubled teenagers, there is no middle ground between a broken home and a prison cell. In this sobering look inside the juvenile justice system, we follow Carlton, a repeat offender facing his harshest sentence yet: a transfer to the Department of Corrections' notorious "Boy School." From the anxiety of the early morning transport to the stark reality of the intake strip-search, we see firsthand what happens when the streets catch up to kids as young as twelve. Alongside Paradize, a 15-year-old girl who cut off her ankle monitor to escape her family struggles, these raw human stories reveal the tragic pipeline from childhood trauma to maximum security confinement—and the desperate struggle to find a way out before "The Big House" claims them forever.
